# a11y.landmarks — Page does not have exactly one main landmark

- **Check ID:** `a11y.landmarks`
- **Default severity:** `warning`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** WCAG 1.3.1, WCAG 2.4.1
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/a11y.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/a11y.landmarks.md`](../a11y.landmarks.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

A page has no `<main>` landmark, or has more than one visible one.

## Why it matters

Screen reader users move around a page by jumping between landmarks: banner, navigation, main, footer. The `main` landmark is the one that takes them past the repeated header and menu straight to what is new on this page, which satisfies the "bypass blocks" requirement. A page without it forces them through everything above the content, on every page. Two visible `main` landmarks make that shortcut ambiguous.

## What it checks

- **No main** (warning): a page that has some text in its `<body>` and no visible `<main>` element or `role="main"` element. Redirect stubs (`html.meta-refresh`) and pages without text are skipped.
- **More than one main** (warning): every visible `main` after the first. HTML allows several `<main>` elements only when all but one carry the `hidden` attribute, so hidden ones, and ones inside `hidden` or `aria-hidden="true"` content, are not counted.

## How to fix

```html
<!-- before -->
<body>
  <nav>...</nav>
  <div class="content"><h1>Pricing</h1>...</div>
</body>

<!-- after -->
<body>
  <nav>...</nav>
  <main><h1>Pricing</h1>...</main>
</body>
```

Wrap the part that is different on each page, and leave the site header, navigation, and footer outside it. Static site generators usually do this once in the base layout. There is no automatic edit, because the report cannot know where the content starts and ends.

## Options

None.
